question: Can the Supreme Court exercise powers under Article 142 of the Constitution to grant admission to an IIT candidate from a marginalized community who was prevented from paying fees due to a portal login glitch?
answer_text: The Supreme Court can exercise powers under Article 142 for remedial measures in cases where individuals are unable to perform their legal obligations due to circumstances beyond their control. [E1]. In the case of Atul Kumar, despite taking all steps required by IIT's formalities for admission and facing a portal login glitch that prevented timely fee payment, his situation falls under circumstances where Article 142 can be invoked. [E1].
claim_sentence: The Supreme Court can exercise powers under Article 142 for remedial measures in cases where individuals are unable to perform their legal obligations due to circumstances beyond their control.

supporting_passages.case_title: ATUL KUMAR versus THE CHAIRMAN (JOINT SEAT ALLOCATION AUTHORITY) AND OTHERS
supporting_passages.passage_text:
[2024] 10 S.C.R. 150 : 2024 INSC 749
Atul Kumar 
v. 
The Chairman (Joint Seat Allocation Authority) and Others
(Writ Petition (Civil) No 609 of 2024)
30 September 2024
[Dr Dhananjaya Y Chandrachud, CJI, J B Pardiwala and 
Manoj Misra, JJ.]
Issue for Consideration
Matter pertains to Schedule caste category student who lost his 
admission to IIT since he was late in paying the online admission 
fee of Rs 17,500/- by a few minutes.
Headnotes†
Constitution of India – Art. 142 – Exercise of power under – 
Indian Institute of Technology IIT-Admission – Schedule 
caste category student allotted seat in Electrical Engineering 
course at IIT – Took all steps to comply with all formalities 
pursuant to the allotment to him of a seat for the course, 
however, lost his admission to IIT since he was late in paying 
the online admission fee of Rs 17,500/- by a few minutes – 
Challenge to:
Held: Petitioner logged in as many as on six occasions and 
uploaded the documents, which evidently indicates that he was 
making earnest efforts to log into the portal – No conceivable 
reason why the petitioner would not have done so if he had the 
wherewithal to pay the fees of Rs 17,500 – Talented student like 
the petitioner who belongs to a marginalized group of citizens 
and has done everything to secure admission should not be left 
in the lurch – Power of this Court u/Art.142 to do substantial 
justice is meant precisely to cover such a situation – Petitioner 
to be granted admission to IIT Dhanbad against the seat which 
was allotted to him in the branch of Electrical Engineering  – 
Supernumerary seat to be created for the petitioner, if so 
required. [Paras 6, 7]
List of Acts
Constitution of India.

question: Does an appeal lie to the Supreme Court under Section 62 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code against an order of the NCLAT approving withdrawal of CIRP under Rule 11?
answer_text: An appeal lies under Section 62 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code against an order from NCLAT. [E1].
claim_sentence: An appeal lies under Section 62 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code against an order from NCLAT.

prescribed procedure for withdrawal of Corporate Insolvency 
Resolution Process (CIRP) and settlement of claims between

while exercising its discretionary power under Rule 11 of the

question: Is a specific and clear entry in the balance sheet of a Corporate Debtor required to constitute an acknowledgment of debt under Section 18 of the Limitation Act for IBC proceedings?
answer_text: A specific and clear acknowledgement of debt by Corporate Debtor in its balance sheet entries constitutes an admission necessary for limitation proceedings under Section 18 of the Limitation Act. [E1].
claim_sentence: A specific and clear acknowledgement of debt by Corporate Debtor in its balance sheet entries constitutes an admission necessary for limitation proceedings under Section 18 of the Limitation Act.

question: Can an authorized signatory who signs a cheque on behalf of a company be directed to deposit an interim sum under Section 148 of the Negotiable Instruments Act upon appeal against conviction under Section 138?
answer_text: An authorized signatory can be directed to deposit an interim sum as per Section 148 upon appeal. [E1].
claim_sentence: An authorized signatory can be directed to deposit an interim sum as per Section 148 upon appeal.

supporting_passages.passage_text:

Issue for Consideration
Whether the signatory of a cheque authorized by the Company 
is a drawer and whether such a signatory could be directed to 
deposit any sum out of the fine or compensation awarded by the 
trial Court u/s.148 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, as a 
condition for suspending the sentence in an appeal filed against 
his conviction u/s.138 of the NI Act.
Headnotes†

is the authorized signatory of the company – The signed 
cheques were presented in the bank – The cheques were 
dishonoured and returned with the endorsement “payment 
stopped by the drawer” – Trial Court found appellant guilty 
and accordingly was convicted and sentenced – Appellant filed 
criminal appeals before the Principal City Civil and Session 
Judge – The sentence was suspended with condition to 
deposit 20% of the fine/compensation – It is against the said 
direction to deposit 20% of the compensation amount that

question: Are prison rules that assign manual labour and segregated duties according to the caste of inmates constitutional under Articles 14 and 15 of the Constitution?
answer_text: Prison manual assignments based on caste are unconstitutional. [E1]. The court found the ‘habitual offenders’ criteria in prison rules to be constitutionally problematic, implying a broader issue with discrimination based on caste within penal institutions. [E1].
claim_sentence: Prison manual assignments based on caste are unconstitutional.
